What Caused Bitcoin’s Flash Crash on Kraken?
A flash crash is a sudden, extreme price drop that quickly reverses. It usually happens when thin order books meet heavy selling.
on every major exchange and USD pair. Only the BTC/CAD order book collapsed, as few buyers stepped in to absorb the selling.
Thin weekend liquidity met a wave of aggressive market sells.
As a result, the pair fell to C$24,250 (about $16,900), nearly 70% below the real market price.
“Its their USDCAD pair that depegged, and all CAD pairs via arb accordingly,” Adam Back said.

children: No. According to Kraken, heavy selling pressure hit its CAD pairs starting around 20:00 UTC on Friday.
“Our platform processed every order correctly,” the exchange said. It added that its security teams found “no sign of a breach or compromised accounts.” Moreover, “executed trades stand.”
That means every order filled at those extreme prices remains valid.
Traders who bought and withdrew during the window secured life-changing discounts. In contrast, sellers who panicked or got liquidated absorbed heavy losses.
By midday, the pair snapped back above C$80,000 (roughly $55,800) as liquidity returned.
Therefore, the event never reflected Bitcoin’s true market value.
Even so, the broader market has not escaped the pressure. Bitcoin fell to nearly $55,000 across major exchanges before recovering toward $60,800 in recent hours.

Still, the episode offers a stark reminder. Even the largest platforms can produce extreme price anomalies when order books run dry. For traders, thin fiat pairs can carry hidden risks, especially on weekends.

title: Bitcoin Crashes to $17,000 This Weekend: Inside the Bizarre Flash Crash Mystery
